name: Data Filtering
apex: BOSS REST Data Sources delegate end-user search/filter to the server via BOSS filter predicates; regions can add an External Filter using SQL-like syntax over case-sensitive attribute names.
workflow: Developer writes a BOSS filter predicate in region settings or an URL Pattern parameter, optionally substituting APEX page items with &P3_NAME.
relevance: Paddock has no BOSS/Oracle Fusion backend; filtering happens against Supabase/snapshot data with normal SQL, not a remote object-service filter language.
skip_for_web: Entire BOSS filter-predicate mechanism is Oracle Cloud SaaS specific.

name: Data Ordering
apex: BOSS REST Data Sources delegate end-user sort to the server; regions can set an External Order Bys clause listing attribute:asc/desc pairs.
workflow: Developer supplies a comma-separated sort expression when a BOSS attribute isn't natively sortable through the endpoint.
relevance: No BOSS endpoint in Paddock; sorting is done in SQL/JS over local data already.
skip_for_web: BOSS-specific server-side sort delegation.

name: Lost Update Protection
apex: Optimistic-concurrency check APEX runs before saving edited/deleted rows from a BOSS source, re-fetching each row by key (or by ETag/row-version column) to detect concurrent changes.
attributes: Lost Update Type = Row Version Column
workflow: Developer sets Lost Update Type to Row Version Column and names APEX$ETAG as the version column when the BOSS object exposes an ETag.
relevance: Generic optimistic-concurrency concept is sound but Paddock's admin writes go through its own Supabase update calls, not a generated BOSS-backed grid; no equivalent mechanism to copy.
skip_for_web: Mechanism is wired specifically to BOSS ETag semantics.

name: ETag Support
apex: When a BOSS object has a versionNumber history attribute, APEX exposes it as an APEX$ETAG data-profile column and automatically sends it on update/delete so BOSS can do server-side concurrency checks.
workflow: Developer includes APEX$ETAG in the region's columns and sets it as the row version column, or disables APEX-side lost-update checks entirely and lets BOSS handle it.
relevance: Purely a BOSS/Oracle Fusion contract; Paddock has no ETag-bearing upstream objects.
skip_for_web: BOSS-specific.

name: Bulk DML
apex: By default APEX batches all inserts/updates/deletes from one Save into a single round trip to the BOSS REST endpoint; can be disabled per data source if the endpoint mishandles batching, and must be disabled for nested child resources.
workflow: Developer flips Use Bulk DML to No when a BOSS endpoint doesn't support bulk operations or when the source is a nested child resource.
relevance: Bulk batching of writes to a remote business-object API has no counterpart in Paddock's architecture (loader is the only writer, admin writes are simple single-row Supabase calls).
skip_for_web: BOSS bulk-operation plumbing.

name: Validation Errors Display as APEX Errors Automatically
apex: Server-side validation failures raised by a BOSS business object's rules/triggers surface automatically as standard APEX page error messages, one per line, when a region based on that data source is saved.
workflow: No developer setup needed; automatic pass-through of BOSS validation messages into APEX's normal error UI.
relevance: General idea (surface backend validation errors in the same UI as local ones) is unremarkable and Paddock already does this in its own API routes; nothing BOSS-specific to copy.
skip_for_web: BOSS-specific error propagation.

name: Filter Parameters for Query By Example and Parent/Child Use Cases
apex: A BOSS REST Data Source's GET URL Pattern parameters can be named attrName_operator$behavior (operator: eq/contains/startswith; null-behavior: ignoreifnull/norowsifnull/matchifnull) to declaratively drive cascading LOVs and query-by-example pages.
workflow: Developer names a URL parameter per this convention, binds it to a page item's value (directly or as an LOV's parent item), then sets Parent Item on the dependent select list so it re-queries on change.
relevance: The parent/child cascading-select and QBE pattern (child list re-filters when a parent item changes, with explicit null-handling) is a reusable interaction idea for Paddock filters like series to season to round, even though the wire format (BOSS URL params) is not.
skip_for_web: The attrName_operator$behavior URL-parameter naming convention itself is BOSS-specific plumbing.

name: Best Practices for Configuring BOSS REST Service Base URL
apex: Guidance to split a BOSS endpoint URL into a Remote Server Base URL (environment-specific, sticky per deployment target) plus a static Service URL Path, so DEV/PROD deploys swap only the base URL.
workflow: Developer decides which part of the endpoint URL differs between DEV and PROD, puts that in a Remote Server's Base URL, and keeps the rest as Service URL Path on the REST Data Source.
relevance: The idea of separating an environment-varying base host from a fixed path, kept 'sticky' per deployment target, matches how Paddock should treat any future external base URLs across its testing/paris/prod Workers.
skip_for_web: BOSS-specific wizard steps.

name: Using BOSS REST Data Sources in PL/SQL (APEX_EXEC)
apex: APEX_EXEC package lets PL/SQL query, insert, update, and delete rows against a BOSS REST Data Source programmatically (outside of declarative form/grid regions), addressing the source by its static id.
workflow: Developer opens a query or DML context against the data source's static id, loops or sets row values, then executes and closes the context, wrapping in exception handlers that also close the context.
relevance: Paddock has no PL/SQL runtime and no BOSS endpoints; equivalent programmatic data access is plain TypeScript against Supabase, not a cursor-like exec package.
skip_for_web: Entire APEX_EXEC/BOSS PL/SQL API is Oracle-database-specific.

name: Performing DML Operations on Objects with ETags
apex: Restates the ETag/APEX$ETAG column requirement: mandatory in the column list when a BOSS object has historyType='versionNumber', marked as a checksum column programmatically; safe to drop the column when the object has no ETag.
workflow: Developer includes or omits the ETag column depending on whether the BOSS object supports versioning.
relevance: Duplicate of the ETag Support topic; still BOSS-specific and not applicable to Paddock's data layer.
skip_for_web: BOSS-specific.

name: Writing Business Objects with Nested Collections
apex: Shows APEX_EXEC writing a parent business object and nested child array (e.g. an order plus its order lines) in one bulk DML payload, using add_dml_array_row and p_parent_column_path to link child rows to the array column.
workflow: Developer defines a parent column plus array-typed child columns with parent_column_path, adds one parent DML row then one array row per child, and executes in a single call.
relevance: Nested parent/child writes in one call is a reasonable idea in the abstract, but the concrete mechanism (APEX_EXEC array columns against a BOSS endpoint) has no Paddock equivalent; Supabase writes would use ordinary nested inserts/RPC instead.
skip_for_web: APEX_EXEC/BOSS-specific nested array DML API.

name: Invoking BOSS Business Object Custom Actions
apex: BOSS custom actions (server-side operations beyond CRUD) are invoked via a Simple HTTP REST Data Source with manually configured Input Parameters, Request Body Template, and Data Profile, callable from Invoke API page process, a workflow activity, or APEX_EXEC.EXECUTE_REST_SOURCE.
attributes: Simple HTTP REST Data Source type
OUT parameters of type Data Profile Column
workflow: Developer configures a Simple HTTP data source for the custom action's endpoint, maps response fields to Data Profile columns, and calls it declaratively or from PL/SQL.
relevance: Custom remote-procedure-style REST calls are a general pattern, but this is BOSS/Oracle Fusion terminology; Paddock's loader already calls arbitrary REST endpoints in plain TypeScript without needing this abstraction.
skip_for_web: BOSS custom-action invocation is Oracle Cloud SaaS specific.

name: Reading Business Objects with Nested Collections
apex: Data Profile columns of type Array represent nested BOSS collections (e.g. Order to OrderLines to Fulfillments); APEX_EXEC's open_array/next_array_row/close_array let PL/SQL walk a multi-level hierarchy from one query result.
workflow: Developer defines array columns with selectors relative to their parent array, then nests open_array/close_array calls matching the hierarchy depth when reading rows in PL/SQL.
relevance: Nested-collection modeling (parent with child arrays) is a familiar general shape, but Paddock reads nested JSON with plain JS destructuring; no need for a cursor-based array API like APEX_EXEC.
skip_for_web: APEX_EXEC nested array traversal is Oracle-PL/SQL-specific.

name: REST Data Sources Utilization report
apex: A report reachable from the REST Data Sources shared-component page showing everywhere a given REST Data Source is used within the application.
workflow: Developer opens Shared Components > REST Data Sources > Utilization to find all consumers before editing or deleting a source.
relevance: Same generic 'where is this used' safety report pattern already noted for other shared components (lists, LOVs); Paddock Developer should give every shared data source a usage report before allowing deletion.

name: REST Data Sources History report
apex: A report reachable from the REST Data Sources shared-component page listing recent modifications made to REST Data Sources in the current workspace.
workflow: Developer opens Shared Components > REST Data Sources > History to audit recent edits.
relevance: Reinforces the recurring shared-component History/audit-trail pattern; worth a generic 'recent changes' log across Paddock Developer's shared components.

name: REST Source Catalogs
apex: A workspace-level (cross-application) catalog of REST Data Source metadata/templates, organized into Catalog Groups, that any app in the workspace can draw on to create its own REST Data Sources; catalogs can be built manually, generated from an uploaded OpenAPI file, and exported/imported between instances.
attributes: Create from OpenAPI (Upload File / OpenAPI Endpoint URL)
workflow: Developer (in Workspace Utilities) creates a group, creates a catalog by hand or from an OpenAPI spec, then from any REST Data Source clicks Save to Catalog to register it for reuse by other apps.
relevance: A workspace-wide registry of known external data sources (with defaults, auth type, refresh URL) mirrors what Paddock's loader already touches informally (OpenF1, ICS feeds, results scrapers) — Paddock Developer could formalize this as a Data Sources catalog page documenting each upstream, its auth/credential, and refresh cadence, reused by future loader jobs.
skip_for_web: OpenAPI-file catalog generation and cross-instance export/import of catalogs are unneeded; Paddock has one deployment topology, not many APEX instances trading catalogs.

name: About Data Synchronization
apex: Feature that automatically syncs a local database table with data from a REST service (manually or on a scheduler job), so reporting, indexing, PL/SQL processing, and long-time-range aggregation all run against fast local data instead of repeated live HTTP calls.
attributes: local table auto-created from Data Profile's visible columns
manual sync vs scheduled sync (CREATE JOB privilege)
DDL sync statements when table drifts from Data Profile
use cases: large paginated datasets, PL/SQL processing, long time-range merge, faster caching than JSON-CLOB cache
workflow: Developer decides a REST source is high-traffic or needs SQL-side reporting, and turns on synchronization so APEX periodically pulls the endpoint into a real table.
relevance: This IS Paddock's own architecture already: warm-live-data.mts fetches upstreams from a clean IP and persists snapshots to Supabase/tables that the Worker reads at request time, avoiding live upstream calls — APEX's stated rationale (pagination cost, indexing, longer time ranges, avoiding repeated JSON parsing) is the same justification Paddock already uses; validates the design and suggests documenting it in the same explicit terms (merge-by-key, schedule, local table as source of truth).
skip_for_web: The APEX-specific screens (Local Table Owner, DBMS_SCHEDULER calendaring syntax) are not needed since Paddock's sync is a GitHub Actions script, not a DB-scheduler job.

name: Configuring REST Synchronization
apex: Per-REST-Data-Source settings page (Manage Synchronization) defining the target local table, how rows land in it, and the run schedule/limits.
attributes: Synchronize to: New Table / Existing Table
Synchronization Schedule (DBMS_SCHEDULER calendar syntax, Interval Builder)
Steps (Add Step to pass parameters/external filters per invocation)
workflow: Developer points a REST Data Source at a new or existing table, picks Append/Merge/Replace semantics (Merge needs a Primary Key), sets a schedule or Steps for multi-call syncs, then Saves or Save and Runs.
relevance: The three sync semantics (Append/Merge-by-key/Replace-all) and the Steps concept (invoke once per parameter set, e.g. once per season) are a clean vocabulary Paddock's loader already implements ad hoc; worth adopting the same Append/Merge/Replace naming when documenting or building a Data Sources admin screen.
skip_for_web: Scheduler-calendar syntax, commit-interval/HTTP-limit tuning are DB-scheduler execution details Paddock's GitHub Actions cron doesn't need.

name: REST Synchronization management (import behavior, usage report, log, purge)
apex: Supporting admin around synchronization: imported apps have sync disabled by default (re-enable via apex_rest_source_sync.enable/reschedule to avoid duplicate concurrent runs), a Synchronize Usage report lists components reading the local table, Clear Settings reverts components to hit the REST service directly, and a purgeable Synchronization Log records status/row counts/HTTP request counts per run with drill-down to the Web Services log.
attributes: Synchronization Log (status, rows processed, HTTP requests)
workflow: Developer re-enables sync after an app import, audits which regions depend on the local table before changing sync settings, and reviews/purges the run log for failures.
relevance: The run-log pattern (status, row count, request count per execution) is exactly the kind of visibility Paddock's warm-live-data.mts runs should expose in a Data Sources health page; the 'usage report before changing a source' safety check echoes the Utilization pattern seen elsewhere.
skip_for_web: Import/export-triggered auto-disable and apex_rest_source_sync PL/SQL calls are Oracle-instance-specific.

name: Managing REST Enabled SQL References (overview)
apex: A REST Enabled SQL reference lets an APEX component run SQL or PL/SQL against a remote database over REST (via ORDS on that remote DB), rather than reading a JSON payload shaped by a REST Data Source's Data Profile.
attributes: Understanding REST Enabled SQL Service References
Creating/Updating Components to Use a REST Enabled SQL
workflow: Developer registers a reference to a remote ORDS-enabled schema, then points reports/forms/charts/calendars/trees at it instead of a local table.
relevance: Requires a second Oracle Database instance running ORDS; Paddock's only database is its own Supabase Postgres queried directly, so there is no 'remote SQL over REST' problem to solve.
skip_for_web: Entire feature is Oracle-to-Oracle (or Oracle-to-MySQL-via-ORDS) cross-database SQL tunneling.

name: REST Enabled SQL Service Requirements
apex: Before creating a reference, the remote database must run Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) 20.x+ with REST Enabled SQL turned on, and the target schema activated via ords.enable_schema, producing an endpoint URL shaped http://host:port/ords/schema.
workflow: DBA/developer runs ords.enable_schema on the remote schema, then feeds the resulting URL into APEX's REST Enabled SQL reference.
relevance: No remote Oracle/ORDS estate exists or is planned for Paddock.
skip_for_web: ORDS-specific setup.

name: Creating a REST Enabled SQL Service Reference
apex: Wizard (Workspace Utilities or Shared Components > REST Enabled SQL Databases) that names the reference, takes the ORDS endpoint URL, and collects Basic or OAuth2 Client credentials, testing the connection on Create.
attributes: Authentication Type: Basic Authentication / OAuth2 Client
workflow: Developer supplies the ORDS URL and credentials; APEX immediately test-connects and reports success/failure.
relevance: Same ORDS-only feature; not applicable without a remote ORDS-enabled database.
skip_for_web: ORDS/remote-schema specific.

name: About REST Enabled SQL Service References / MySQL Support
apex: A workspace-level reference that lets any app run arbitrary SQL/PL/SQL on a remote Oracle or MySQL database fronted by ORDS 23.3+, returning self-describing JSON (metadata, rows, pagination); usable from most report/form/chart/calendar/tree components and PL/SQL, but MySQL targets are read-only with many unsupported features (DML, some aggregates, Flashback, BLOB columns, multi-value facets, etc.).
attributes: RESTful Services enabled at workspace/instance level
MySQL: read-only, no DML, limited aggregates/Flashback/BLOB
workflow: Developer defines the reference once per remote schema, then any component can query it like a data source.
relevance: No remote Oracle/MySQL database with ORDS exists for Paddock; direct Supabase Postgres access already covers this need.
skip_for_web: Cross-database remote-SQL-over-REST is irrelevant to a single-Postgres content site.

name: Differences between REST Enabled SQL Service References and Database Links
apex: Contrasts two remote-data mechanisms: database links work at the SQL level (can join remote+local tables in one query) over SQL*Net, which struggles over the internet/cloud; REST Enabled SQL works at the workspace level over JSON/HTTPS (cloud-friendly) but cannot join to local tables in the same query. Both are slower than a local table, so Oracle recommends replicating remote data locally with a refresh algorithm whenever page performance matters.
attributes: REST Enabled SQL: workspace-level, JSON over HTTP(S), no join to local tables
workflow: Developer picks database link only when both databases are Oracle and reachable over SQL*Net; otherwise uses REST Enabled SQL for internet/cloud reach, but is steered toward local replication for performance-sensitive pages.
relevance: The closing guidance — any live remote fetch is slower than a local table, so replicate with a refresh algorithm when performance matters — is the exact justification for Paddock's loader-to-Supabase-snapshot design; good corroborating language for documenting why Paddock never queries upstreams at request time.
skip_for_web: The database-link mechanism itself (Oracle-to-Oracle SQL*Net) has no Paddock equivalent.

name: Populating the Endpoint URL Dynamically (Flexible Remote Server) / Export-Import
apex: A Remote Server's Configuration Procedure attribute can run a small PL/SQL callback at request time to compute the Endpoint URL's base_url and #placeholder# substitutions from session state, app ID, or a config table, cached for the rest of that request; exporting an app carries along used REST Enabled SQL references, deduped by static ID on import.
workflow: Developer writes a procedure that branches on APP_ID/session state and sets p_config.base_url, then wires it into the Remote Server's Configuration Procedure field.
relevance: Paddock resolves base URLs from static per-Worker environment variables (wrangler.jsonc / wrangler.testing.jsonc / wrangler.paris.jsonc) at deploy time, not a runtime PL/SQL callback per request; no equivalent need.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL runtime callback mechanism is Oracle-specific.

name: Example: Creating a REST Enabled SQL Service Reference (Oracle and MySQL)
apex: Two worked examples of the Create wizard: an Oracle target (Basic Auth with upper-cased or !-escaped username) and a MySQL target, which adds a Store Credentials toggle (leaving it off requires runtime APEX_CREDENTIAL.SET_SESSION_CREDENTIALS), a Case Sensitive User Name switch (MySQL usernames are typically lower-case), and a post-create Set Default Database step.
workflow: Developer fills the same General/Authentication wizard as the base Create flow, with MySQL needing the extra case-sensitivity and default-database choices.
relevance: No remote Oracle/MySQL+ORDS target exists for Paddock.
skip_for_web: ORDS/ MySQL-specific wizard nuances.

name: Editing a REST Enabled SQL Service Reference
apex: Edit page for a REST Enabled SQL reference, adding session-lifecycle hooks (code to run before/after the component SQL executes) and a Static ID plus Server Time Zone used to decode DATE/TIMESTAMP values from the remote service.
workflow: Developer edits connection/auth fields, optionally adds init/cleanup PL/SQL around each query, and confirms with Save and Test.
relevance: No PL/SQL runtime or remote-SQL session lifecycle exists in Paddock's Next.js/Supabase stack.
skip_for_web: Session init/cleanup code hooks are specific to the REST-Enabled-SQL connection model.

name: Deleting / Utilization / History for REST Enabled SQL Services
apex: Standard trio: Delete is blocked while any component still uses the reference; Utilization lists where it's used workspace-wide; History lists recent edits — mirroring the same reports every other shared component type gets.
workflow: Developer checks Utilization before attempting Delete, which fails while a component still references the service.
relevance: Reconfirms the recurring 'block delete while referenced, show a usage report first' safety pattern Paddock Developer should apply uniformly to every shared/reusable object (data sources, lists, LOVs, etc.), independent of the REST-Enabled-SQL specifics.
skip_for_web: The specific object type (REST Enabled SQL) is not needed.

name: Creating or Updating Components to Use a REST Enabled SQL (overview)
apex: Index page listing that reports, charts, calendars, and existing components can all be pointed at a REST Enabled SQL reference instead of a local table.
attributes: Specifying a reference in an existing component
workflow: Developer picks the REST Enabled SQL reference as the row source when creating or editing these region types.
relevance: Just a table of contents for the Oracle/MySQL-only feature; no new pattern.

name: Creating Report/Chart/Calendar Using a REST Enabled SQL Reference, and Retrofitting Existing Components
apex: In the Create Page Wizard (Interactive Report, Chart, Calendar) or in an existing region's Property Editor, choosing Data Source/Source Location = REST Enabled SQL, picking a previously defined reference, then Source Type Table/View or SQL Query, makes that component read from the remote database exactly like a local one.
attributes: Source Type: Table/View vs SQL Query
calendar: Display Column / Start Date Column / End Date Column / Show Time
workflow: Developer either builds a new page choosing REST Enabled SQL as the data source in the wizard, or edits an existing region's Source, Location property to point at the reference instead of Local Database.
relevance: Every one of these flows assumes a remote Oracle/MySQL database reachable via ORDS; Paddock's regions read Supabase/local snapshot data directly, so there is no 'switch a region's source to a remote database' feature to replicate.
skip_for_web: ORDS-backed remote source selection across report/chart/calendar wizards.

name: Remote Servers (concept)
apex: A workspace-level object storing the server/base-URL part of an endpoint (host, port, path prefix) separately from the REST-Data-Source-specific path; one Remote Server can back many REST Data Sources (and Authentication, Print Server, or File Server uses), so changing its Base URL moves every dependent source from test to production in one edit.
attributes: Server Type: REST Data Source / Authentication / Print Server / File Server
workflow: Developer creates one Remote Server per external host, then builds multiple REST Data Sources against paths under it; promoting environments means editing only the Remote Server's URL.
relevance: Directly useful shape for a Paddock 'Data Sources' registry: define each upstream host (OpenF1, an ICS calendar host, a results-scrape host) once, let every consuming loader job/config reference it, and change one field to repoint an entire family of sources between environments.
skip_for_web: The 'Server Type: Authentication/Print/File Server' variants are APEX-runtime concepts Paddock has no use for.

name: Creating / Editing a Remote Server
apex: Create/Edit form for a Remote Server: General section names it and sets its type and Endpoint URL (with an install-time prompt option); Advanced section adds a Static Identifier for API/reference use and optional PL/SQL-driven dynamic URL resolution.
workflow: Developer names the server, sets its base URL and type, and reuses its Static Identifier when defining REST Data Sources against it; cannot delete while any REST Data Source still points to it.
relevance: Straightforward attribute checklist Paddock Developer could copy verbatim for a Data Source/Remote registry entry (name, static id, base URL, environment-prompt flag, comments, delete-guard).
skip_for_web: PL/SQL Code / Configuration Procedure fields (dynamic runtime URL) are unneeded — Paddock resolves base URLs at deploy time via env vars.

name: Flexible Remote Servers (dynamic Endpoint URL) / Export-Import
apex: Same Configuration Procedure callback mechanism as REST Enabled SQL's Flexible Remote Server, generalized to any REST Data Source or Authentication-type Remote Server: a PL/SQL procedure sets p_config.base_url and #placeholder# substitutions at request time, cached per request; exported apps carry Remote Servers, deduped on import by Static ID.
workflow: Developer writes a procedure branching on APP_ID/session/config table to compute the base URL dynamically instead of hard-coding it.
relevance: Duplicate of the REST-Enabled-SQL Flexible Remote Server mechanism; Paddock still has no per-request dynamic base URL need.
skip_for_web: Runtime PL/SQL URL resolution.

name: Remote Server Utilization / History reports
apex: Same recurring pair of reports for Remote Servers: Utilization shows where a server is used workspace-wide, History shows recent modifications.
workflow: Developer checks Utilization before editing/deleting a shared Remote Server.
relevance: Further confirms the standard usage-report-plus-audit-log pairing Paddock Developer should give every shared/reusable object, not just this one.

name: Web Credentials (concept) / Protecting by Valid URLs
apex: Workspace-level, write-only-encrypted store of authentication material for REST calls, visible to all apps in the workspace; an optional Valid for URLs list on each credential restricts which endpoint prefixes it may ever be sent to, and APEX raises a runtime error if a request URL doesn't match, preventing a credential from leaking to the wrong host.
attributes: encrypted, never retrievable in clear text
Valid for URLs (one URL prefix per line)
runtime error: Credential is not allowed to be used for this URL endpoint
workflow: Developer creates one credential object per external service and optionally locks it to that service's URL prefix(es) so a misconfigured data source can't exfiltrate it elsewhere.
relevance: The Valid-for-URLs binding is a concrete, adoptable safety pattern: if Paddock Developer ever lets an operator store a third-party API key for a curated data source, scoping that secret to an allow-listed URL prefix (checked before every outbound call) meaningfully reduces SSRF/leak risk.
skip_for_web: Nothing to skip; the pattern is lightweight and framework-agnostic.

name: Supported Authentication Types in Web Credentials
apex: Catalog of credential shapes a Web Credential can hold: Basic Authentication, OAuth2 Client Credentials (with transparent token refresh), OCI Native Authentication, HTTP Header, URL Query String (API-key style), OAuth2 Password Flow, Signed User Assertion (JWT asserting current user, needs a Trusted OAuth client), its companion User Assertion Signing Certificate, Key Pair, and Certificate Pair (SAML).
workflow: Developer picks the auth type matching the target API's requirements when creating the credential; APEX handles token exchange/refresh transparently for the OAuth2 types.
relevance: Useful minimal vocabulary if Paddock Developer ever needs to store more than a bearer token for a curated source: Basic/Header/Query-string/OAuth2-client-credentials cover essentially every REST API auth style Paddock is likely to meet; the transparent-refresh-on-expiry behavior for OAuth2 is worth copying if a token-based upstream is added.
skip_for_web: OCI Native, Signed User Assertion, Key/Certificate Pair (SAML) are enterprise-identity specific and have no Paddock use case.

name: Using a Database Credential with Web Credentials
apex: On Oracle Database 26ai/Autonomous 19c+, a Basic Authentication or OAuth2 Client Credentials Web Credential can delegate its secret storage to a database credential (DBMS_CREDENTIAL/DBMS_CLOUD); requests then run under the app's parsing schema (needing PL/SQL network ACLs) and APEX cannot enforce Valid for URLs since it never sees the secret.
workflow: DBA maintains the credential at the database layer; APEX just references it by name.
relevance: Oracle-Database-specific credential delegation; Paddock's secrets already live in Cloudflare's secret store / env vars, not a database credential object.
skip_for_web: Entire database-credential integration is Oracle-only.

name: Creating Web Credentials — common fields and Basic/OAuth2 Client Credentials
apex: Create form: Name, Static ID, and Authentication Type are common to every type; secrets (Client Secret/Password/Private Key) are always write-only with a Verify field for double entry, never exported in clear text, while non-secret identifiers (Client ID/Username) are unencrypted and DO get an install-time prompt. OAuth2 Client Credentials adds OAuth Scope, Token Authentication Method (how Client ID/Secret are sent: Basic header, Basic header + body Client ID, both in body, or Client ID only in body), and Named Scopes (aliases for scope values); a Use Database Credential switch (Basic/OAuth2 CC only) delegates secret storage to the database instead.
workflow: Developer names the credential, picks its type, fills type-specific fields, and always re-enters any secret to confirm it before saving.
relevance: The write-only-secret + mandatory verify-field + auto-generated install-time prompt pattern is a solid, reusable form design for any 'store an API key' UI Paddock Developer builds for curated data sources; the 4 Token-Authentication-Method variants are a good checklist if Paddock ever adds OAuth2-client-credentials support for an upstream.
skip_for_web: OAuth2 mechanics beyond client-credentials (Password flow, scopes) exceed anything Paddock's upstreams currently require.

name: Creating Web Credentials — remaining types (OCI, HTTP Header, URL Query String, OAuth2 Password Flow, Signed User Assertion, Key/Certificate Pair)
apex: Type-specific field sets: OCI Native needs User OCID/Private Key/Tenancy ID/Public Key Fingerprint; HTTP Header and URL Query String just need a Credential Name (header or param name) and Credential Secret; OAuth2 Password Flow layers a Basic-Authentication sub-credential for the end-user's username/password on top of a client ID/secret; Signed User Assertion/User Assertion Signing Certificate hold PEM certificates/keys, an Audience List, and a Certificate Alias for JWT signing; Key Pair and Certificate Pair (SAML-only) hold raw public/private key or certificate material.
attributes: OCI User ID / Private Key / Tenancy ID / Public Key Fingerprint
Credential Name / Credential Secret (Header, Query String)
OAuth2 Password Flow Authentication Credential (nested Basic credential)
Signing Credential / Private Key / Audience List / Certificate Alias / Username Expression
workflow: Developer selects the type matching the target API and fills only the fields that type requires; the form reshapes per type.
relevance: None of these enterprise-identity credential shapes (OCI, SAML, signed JWT assertions) have a plausible Paddock use case; the simplest two (HTTP Header, URL Query String) are already implicitly covered by Paddock just reading an env var into a fetch call.
skip_for_web: Enterprise auth types (OCI/SAML/JWT assertion) entirely out of scope.

name: Editing or Deleting Credentials
apex: Standard edit/delete page for a Web Credential; delete is blocked while the credential is referenced anywhere in the workspace.
workflow: Developer edits fields or deletes only after confirming nothing still points at the credential.
relevance: Same delete-guard pattern as every other shared object; reinforces it should be uniform in Paddock Developer.

name: Viewing Credential Utilization / History
apex: Utilization report splits credentials into a used list (with consuming component type, app id, component name) and an unused list at the bottom, with a one-click Delete Unused to bulk-clean stale secrets; History lists recent credential edits.
attributes: Used credentials list (component type, app id, component name)
workflow: Developer periodically opens Utilization to spot and bulk-delete credentials nothing references anymore.
relevance: The used/unused split plus a one-click 'Delete Unused' is a genuinely good secret-hygiene feature worth copying for any Paddock Developer credential or API-key store, since stale secrets are a real risk a plain list won't surface.

name: Generative AI Service (concept)
apex: A workspace-level object (like Remote Servers/Credentials) that pairs an AI provider + base URL + Web Credential into one named service; every AI-powered component or PL/SQL call routes through it, so switching model/provider later is a config edit, not a code change. Rationale given: pick the right model per task, future-proof against fast-moving models, support local/hybrid LLMs (Ollama) for sensitive workloads, and keep secrets server-side only.
workflow: Developer creates one service per provider/model combo they want available, then any AI feature in the app references it by name instead of embedding provider-specific call code.
relevance: Good abstraction to copy if Paddock Developer ever exposes an admin-facing 'AI Assist' feature: one server-side service object (provider, key, model) that every assist feature calls through, instead of hardcoding a provider SDK in each feature.
skip_for_web: Nothing to skip in the concept itself; only the deep provider-specific wiring below is APEX runtime plumbing.

name: Supported AI Providers
apex: APEX normalizes calls to OpenAI, Cohere, OCI Generative AI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Mistral AI, local Ollama, and any generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint behind one internal request/response shape, translating to each provider's real payload/auth (e.g. Claude: messages-based API, x-api-key header; Gemini: API key as query param; OpenAI: Bearer token) and normalizing the reply back.
attributes: Google Gemini (generateContent/embedContent, API key query param)
workflow: Developer just picks a provider from a list; APEX's normalization layer handles the wire-format differences.
relevance: Confirms Claude is a first-class, directly-callable provider in this model (matches the real Claude Messages API shape); the 'generic OpenAI-compatible' fallback is a good extensibility idea to note if Paddock ever builds its own thin AI-provider abstraction rather than hardcoding one SDK.
skip_for_web: Provider-specific payload mapping details (Gemini contents[]/parts[], Cohere fields) are implementation detail Paddock would only need if it built the same abstraction, which is not currently planned.

name: Creating a Generative AI Service (attributes and runtime flow)
apex: Create/Edit form collecting Identification (AI Provider, Name), Settings (Used by App Builder, Default for New Apps, Base URL), Credentials (Web Credential or inline API Key, with a Test Connection check), and Advanced settings (Static ID for APEX_AI.CHAT, AI Model, Maximum AI Tokens per 24h with APEX_AI.GET_AVAILABLE_TOKENS to query remaining budget, custom HTTP Headers, Comments, Additional Attributes merged into the request JSON).
workflow: Developer fills identity/settings/credentials, clicks Test Connection to confirm before saving, and optionally caps daily token spend.
relevance: The per-service 24-hour token budget plus a function to query remaining tokens is a concrete, worth-copying governance pattern if Paddock's own admin ever calls an LLM API server-side and wants to cap spend/abuse.
skip_for_web: APEX_AI.CHAT PL/SQL specifics are Oracle-only.

name: Used by App Builder setting / design-time AI features
apex: Marking one Generative AI Service per workspace as 'Used by App Builder' turns on APEX's own AI-assisted authoring: Create App Using Generative AI, a Generative AI tab in Create Page, natural-language search in interactive reports, and APEX Assistant chat inside code editors.
attributes: Used by App Builder (one per workspace)
natural language support in interactive reports
workflow: Administrator/developer designates one configured service as the App-Builder-facing one; APEX's own wizards then call it to scaffold apps/pages/queries from prose.
relevance: This is APEX's equivalent of an IDE copilot for building the app itself — for Paddock, Claude Code already fills that role at the tooling layer; there is no in-house 'App Builder' whose own UI needs an embedded AI-scaffolding feature.
skip_for_web: Design-time AI scaffolding of the builder itself doesn't apply outside APEX's own IDE.

name: Editing / Deleting / Utilization / History for Generative AI Services
apex: Edit repeats the create form with Test Connection available again; Delete is blocked while in use and, when allowed, leaves the auto-created Web Credential behind for manual cleanup; Utilization and History are the same standard reports as every other shared object.
workflow: Developer deletes an unused AI Service, then separately remembers to delete its now-orphaned Web Credential.
relevance: The 'deleting the parent object leaves a dangling credential behind' gotcha is a concrete lesson: any Paddock Developer feature that auto-creates a secret alongside a config object should either cascade-delete it or warn explicitly, not leave it silently orphaned.

name: Using APEX Assistant
apex: An in-IDE AI chat panel available in every APEX Code Editor once a Generative AI Service is marked Used by App Builder; Query Builder mode answers schema-aware SQL requests, General Assistance mode offers Use/Improve/Explain Selection and 'Help me fix this' on validation errors, and the chat keeps context until Clear Chat, with a mandatory consent dialog on first use and a caution to review AI-generated code before use.
attributes: Help me fix this (on SQL errors)
workflow: Developer opens APEX Assistant from a code editor's menu bar, picks a mode, and iterates in a persistent chat until clearing it.
relevance: This is APEX's IDE-embedded coding copilot — Paddock's equivalent is Claude Code itself, used directly by the developer outside the deployed app; the shipped Paddock site has no code editor needing an embedded assistant.
skip_for_web: Entire feature is a code-authoring aid inside the App Builder IDE.

name: Including Generative AI in Applications — Show AI Assistant vs Generate Text with AI
apex: Two declarative AI-enhanced component shapes: Show AI Assistant (a Dynamic Action True Action) renders a full chat widget as a dialog or inline, configured with a System Prompt, Welcome Message, Initial Prompt, a Use Response mapping (into a page item or JavaScript), and clickable Quick Actions; Generate Text with AI (usable from a Dynamic Action, Page Process, or Workflow Activity) sends one input value to the configured AI service for a single one-shot response (summarize, translate, extract keywords, draft an email), also programmatically reachable via APEX_AI.GENERATE in PL/SQL.
attributes: Show AI Assistant: System Prompt, Welcome Message, Display As (dialog/inline), Initial Prompt, Use Response, Quick Actions
Generate Text with AI: System Prompt, Input Value, Use Response
workflow: Developer adds a True Action of the chosen kind to a button's dynamic action (or a page process/workflow activity), wires an input source and where the response lands.
relevance: The 'Generate Text with AI' one-shot shape (system prompt + input mapping + response mapping, invocable from an action/process) is a clean declarative pattern worth borrowing if Paddock Developer ever adds an admin-side 'draft with AI' action for content fields; the full chat-widget 'Show AI Assistant' is a poorer fit given Paddock's no-AI-phrases editorial voice and anti-chrome design stance.
skip_for_web: Workflow Activity integration and APEX_AI PL/SQL calls are Oracle-runtime specific.

name: Configuring AI Attributes for an Application
apex: An application-level AI tab picks the default Generative AI Service for that app and defines a Consent Message shown to each user the first time they'd use any AI feature; the user's Accept/Deny choice is remembered as a per-user preference (also settable/clearable via APEX_AI programmatically).
workflow: Developer picks the app's default AI service and writes a consent message; APEX gates the first AI interaction on the user accepting it and remembers the answer.
relevance: The explicit, remembered per-user consent gate before any AI feature runs is a directly adoptable pattern for Paddock if it ever ships an AI-touching feature — worth doing regardless of the specific mechanism, for privacy/trust reasons matching the site's editorial, non-hype tone.
skip_for_web: APEX_AI PL/SQL consent API is Oracle-specific plumbing.

name: AI Agent (shared component)
apex: A shared component bundling reusable Generative AI configuration — Service, System Prompt, Welcome Message, Temperature, Response Format (plain Text or a JSON Object matching a supplied JSON Schema), and a set of AI Tools — so multiple Show AI Assistant / Generate Text With AI components (or PL/SQL via APEX_AI) can share one consistent persona/config instead of repeating settings.
attributes: Response Format Type: Text / JSON Object + Schema
workflow: Developer defines one Agent per distinct assistant persona/use case, then points every UI/PLSQL AI call at it instead of duplicating prompt/model settings.
relevance: The 'one shared config object for prompt+model+tools, referenced everywhere' shape is the right architecture if Paddock Developer ever centralizes AI-assist settings, keeping prompts/temperature consistent and editable in one place rather than scattered per feature.
skip_for_web: JSON Schema structured-output mode and PL/SQL-only Agents are deeper than any near-term Paddock need.

name: AI Tool (function-calling / retrieval-augmentation for an Agent)
apex: A named capability attached to an AI Agent, either run automatically before every message (Augment System Prompt, e.g. inject fresh data) or invoked by the model only when it decides it's needed (On Demand, i.e. function-calling), of built-in type Retrieve Data (SQL query / function body / static text, with a token cap), Execute Server-side Code, or Execute Client-side Code (custom types via Tool plug-ins); On Demand tools declare parameters (name, description, data type, required, allowed values) for the model to fill in, can require explicit user confirmation before running, can post a completion notification, and either kind can be gated by a server-side condition on the user's prompt text or by an authorization scheme.
attributes: Execution Point: Augment System Prompt vs On Demand
Type: Retrieve Data / Execute Server-side Code / Execute Client-side Code
Parameters (Name, Description, Data Type, Required, Allowed Values)
workflow: Developer defines a tool's data/action source and, for on-demand tools, its callable signature and any confirmation/authorization gates before the AI Service is allowed to invoke it.
relevance: This is a real, well-designed agentic tool-calling system, but Paddock has no plan for an in-app AI agent that needs to call site functions; the one generically useful idea — require explicit user confirmation before an automated/AI-triggered action with side effects runs — is a general safety principle, not something specific to copy here.
skip_for_web: The entire tool-calling/agent runtime is out of scope absent an actual in-app AI agent feature.

name: Copying/Subscribing to an AI Agent, Utilization, History
apex: Same recurring shared-component trio: Copy an Agent within or from another application (with Subscribe available cross-app), Delete blocked while in use, and Utilization/History reports.
attributes: Copy From: This Application / Other Application
workflow: Developer copies or subscribes to reuse an Agent across apps, and checks Utilization before deleting one.
relevance: Purely a repeat of the copy/subscribe/utilization/history pattern already logged multiple times for other shared components; no new information for Paddock.

name: Worked examples: Dynamic Action Show AI Assistant / Generate Text with AI, and Page Process Generate Text with AI
apex: Three step-by-step walkthroughs wiring a button's Click dynamic action to Show AI Assistant (Agent, Items to Submit feeding session state into the System Prompt/RAG Sources, Display As Dialog/Inline, Quick Actions message) or to Generate Text with AI (System Prompt, Input Value from an item, Use Response into another item), and the same Generate Text with AI logic as an ordinary page process (Sequence, Point, Run Process, Success Message, Error Message/Display Location) instead of a client-side action; a tip recommends a CLOB session-state item when expecting long AI responses.
attributes: Items to Submit (session state feeding the prompt)
Page Process Type = Generate Text with AI
workflow: Developer wires a button click to the chosen AI True Action (or adds an equivalent page process), mapping one page item in and one page item (or CLOB) out.
relevance: Purely restates the already-logged Show AI Assistant / Generate Text with AI shapes in a concrete UI-wiring walkthrough (button, page item in/out) — no new concept beyond ordinary page-process plumbing (Sequence/Point/Success/Error) Paddock would only need if it adopted the AI feature itself.
skip_for_web: Whole click-through is APEX Page-Designer-specific UI wiring.

name: Worked example: AI Assistant to Suggest Salary (end-to-end)
apex: Full tutorial building an HR salary-suggestion chatbot: a hidden item computed via SQL feeds department context into a Static-Value-computed Initial Prompt; the System Prompt hard-codes business rules and a refusal instruction ('only answer questions about salary suggestions'); Initial Prompt + Immediate Action Prompt make the assistant respond proactively without user typing; Use Response's JavaScript Detection Expression regex-extracts just the numeric salary from the AI's free-text reply, and an 'Apply Suggestion' button commits that extracted value into a real page item only on explicit user click.
attributes: System Prompt with hard business rules + explicit refusal instruction
Use Response: Button Label (explicit apply action)
workflow: Developer writes a constrained system prompt, seeds an initial machine-generated prompt from page data, and lets the user explicitly apply a regex-extracted value from the AI's reply rather than auto-saving it.
relevance: The 'AI drafts, regex/rule extracts the structured bit, human clicks Apply before anything is saved' pattern lines up with Paddock's own blog-draft-queue philosophy (never auto-publish, operator always approves) — a reusable interaction shape for any future 'AI-suggested value, human-confirmed' admin field.
skip_for_web: The chat-widget delivery mechanism and constrained-persona system prompt are specific to this narrow tutorial; the underlying idea, not the plumbing, is the transferable part.

name: Accessing Data with Database Links (About / Creating / Viewing)
apex: A database link is an Oracle schema object letting SQL in one database reference objects in another database directly (table@dblink syntax), created and browsed via SQL Workshop's Object Browser; requires the CREATE DATABASE LINK privilege granted by a DBA.
workflow: DBA grants the privilege, developer creates the link in Object Browser, then references remote tables in SQL by appending @dblink.
relevance: SQL-level cross-database joins are an Oracle Database capability with no analogue in Paddock's single-Postgres-via-Supabase-client architecture.
skip_for_web: Entire feature is Oracle-distributed-database specific.

name: Sending Email from an Application (config, provisioning, mail queue, APEX_MAIL)
apex: Outbound email requires an instance administrator to configure SMTP settings and grant network ACLs (DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN) before apps can call the APEX_MAIL package (built on UTL_SMTP); sent mail is queued asynchronously and tracked in a mail queue/log an administrator can monitor, and the same email config can auto-send login credentials when a new workspace is approved.
attributes: Provisioning status: Request with Email Verification
workflow: An instance admin configures SMTP once; developers then just call APEX_MAIL.SEND and monitor delivery via the mail queue/log.
relevance: The account/infrastructure-level SMTP setup and PL/SQL mail package are Oracle-specific; Paddock's contact form already sends mail directly via its own email provider from a Worker route.
skip_for_web: Whole configuration chain (network ACLs, APEX_MAIL, provisioning emails) is Oracle-instance plumbing.

name: Plug-ins (concept) / Implementing Plug-ins overview
apex: A plug-in declaratively extends APEX's built-in component types (item, region, dynamic action, process, authentication/authorization scheme) with a brand-new type that then behaves exactly like a native one in Page Designer; plug-ins are exportable/importable across workspaces and shareable via a public Plug-in Repository. Workflow: create or import a plug-in, use it like any built-in type on a component, then test.
attributes: Type: Item / Region / Dynamic Action / Process / Auth Scheme / Authorization Scheme / Template Component
workflow: Developer builds a plug-in once, then any page in any app in the workspace can create a component of that new type from the standard component gallery, indistinguishable from a built-in one.
relevance: This is the closest APEX concept to Paddock Developer's entire premise — a designer where every page is composed of general, reusable component types. APEX's answer (a registered type with declarative attributes, a settings UI, and render/behavior code, usable everywhere like a built-in) is the architecture to study most closely for Paddock Developer's own component registry.
skip_for_web: The Plug-in Repository (a public marketplace) and cross-workspace export/import have no Paddock equivalent (one codebase, one deployment).

name: Template Component Type Plug-ins
apex: A Template Component is a plug-in built from an HTML markup template with named placeholders (exposed as custom plug-in attributes) instead of PL/SQL rendering code — the fastest way to add a new declarative region/report-row type. Available As controls how it can be used: Multiple (Report, paginated rows), Single (Partial, one row or an interactive-report column), or Region Only (bare HTML, no wrapping chrome, needs an APEX$DOM_ID placeholder). Custom Attributes reference placeholders via #PLACEHOLDER# and can be bulk-generated with Synchronize from Templates; Actions (Button or Menu template, at a chosen Action Position) let end users trigger behavior from the rendered markup; APEX$SELECTOR renders a per-row radio/checkbox when Has Row Selection Support is on; nesting one Template Component inside another uses {with/}...{apply/} template-directive syntax.
attributes: Available As: Multiple (Report) / Single (Partial) / Region Only
workflow: Developer writes an HTML template with placeholders, declares each placeholder as a Custom Attribute so Page Designer exposes it as a settable property, and picks Available As to decide where the component can be dropped.
relevance: This is close to a direct blueprint for Paddock Developer's 'general component' authoring: an HTML-template-plus-named-slots model, with a declarative Available-As classification (list/row/bare-block) and an attribute-to-placeholder binding, is exactly the shape a template-driven component system for a content site would want.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL-based (non-Template-Component) plug-in types remain Oracle-runtime specific, covered separately.

name: Template Component Slots (nesting + type restriction)
apex: Slots are named placeholders in a Template Component's markup where other page components (regions, items, buttons) can be nested; a slot can be restricted to specific component types (e.g. only Checkbox/Radio items, or only Avatar/Static-Content regions) for consistent appearance. Restriction is soft: unsupported types are hidden by default in the Layout tab and Property Editor's Type list but remain reachable via a 'Show Unsupported' toggle, and a developer can still drag an unsupported type in from the Property Editor.
attributes: soft restriction (still movable via Property Editor)
workflow: Developer declares a slot and optionally restricts its allowed child types; Page Designer then defaults new components in that slot to the first allowed type and visually de-emphasizes disallowed ones without hard-blocking power users.
relevance: Directly the pattern Paddock Developer needs for composable regions: a named nesting point that suggests/restricts which component types belong there (e.g. a 'hero' region only accepting certain block types) while still letting an operator override, rather than a rigid hard block — good balance of guardrails and flexibility to copy.

name: Example Template Components (Universal Theme) / Example Plug-ins (community)
apex: Universal Theme ships several ready-made Template Component plug-ins — Comments, Content Row, Media List, Timeline, Metric Card — each a declarative, attribute-driven layout (several supporting avatars/badges) browsable under Shared Components > Templates sorted by Type; separately, APEX World and the Oracle APEX GitHub repo host a broader community/sample plug-in gallery.
attributes: Shared Components > Templates (sort by Type = Template Component)
workflow: Developer browses existing Template Components as a starting point/reference before building a new one from scratch.
relevance: This short list (comments, content row, media list, timeline, metric card) is a good starter checklist of general-purpose block types Paddock Developer's own component registry should probably already cover or plan for on a content site.
skip_for_web: The external community repository (APEX World/GitHub) itself is not applicable.

name: Creating a Plug-in from Scratch
apex: The Create Plug-in wizard: Name plus an auto-generated APEXlang Name (for text-based export) and a Static ID recommended to be reverse-domain-namespaced (e.g. COM.MYCOMPANY.SLIDER) to stay globally unique across shared/imported plug-ins; Type picks which built-in category it extends (Authentication Scheme, Authorization Scheme, Dynamic Action, Generative AI Tool, Item, Process, REST Data Source, Region, Template Component) and reshapes the rest of the form; Source holds the PL/SQL implementation (inline block or a package reference, with a skip-validation-at-create option for performance); Callbacks wires the type-specific render/validate/execute/ajax entry points; Standard Attributes toggles which common property groups the finished component exposes; Information carries Version/About URL/Help Text/Comments for documentation.
attributes: Source: PL/SQL Code or package reference
Do not validate PL/SQL code (runtime-only parse)
Information: Version, About URL, Help Text, Comments
workflow: Developer names and namespaces the plug-in, picks the type it extends, supplies the implementation code and its callback hooks, and turns on the standard attribute groups it should expose in Page Designer.
relevance: The reverse-domain Static ID convention (collision-proofing shared/imported extensions) and the overall shape — name, type, implementation, callback hooks, opt-in standard attribute groups, versioned metadata — is a solid template for how Paddock Developer should register its own general component types.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL Source/Callbacks are Oracle-runtime specific; Paddock components would implement render/behavior in TypeScript/React instead.

name: Standard Attributes for Item Type Plug-ins
apex: A long checklist of opt-in capability flags for an Item-type plug-in, each toggling whether a corresponding property-editor section appears at design time: Is Visible Widget, Standard Form Element (non-standard elements auto-get ARIA-LABELLEDBY for screen readers via APEX_PLUGIN_UTIL.GET_ELEMENT_ATTRIBUTES), Session State Changeable, Has Read Only Attribute, Has Escape Special Characters Attribute, Has Source Attributes (+ Format Mask Date/Number Only), Has Element/Width/Height/Placeholder/Icon Attributes, Has Encrypt Session State Attribute, a full List-of-Values sub-group (Has List of Values, Required, Display Null, Cascading, Join for Column Display), Optional/Always Multiple Values, Has Filter, Has Link, Has Initialization JavaScript Code, and Session State Supports CLOB.
attributes: Has Source Attributes / Format Mask Date or Number Only
Has List of Values (+ Required/Display Null/Cascading/Join)
workflow: Developer checks only the boxes matching what the new item type actually needs, so Page Designer's property panel for it stays minimal and consistent with native items.
relevance: Good checklist for designing Paddock Developer's own component-settings schema: capability flags that gate which editor sections appear (read-only support, LOV binding, width/height, placeholder, icon) map closely onto what a general component's settings panel needs; the auto-injected ARIA-LABELLEDBY for non-standard form elements is a specific accessibility default worth replicating.
skip_for_web: Encrypt-session-state, CLOB session state, and cascading-LOV-join flags are APEX session-state internals with no Paddock analogue.

name: Copying a Plug-in
apex: Create Plug-in wizard's 'As a Copy of an Existing Plug-in' path: pick a source application (and theme, for Template Components), then per-plug-in choose Yes (copy), No (skip), or Copy and Subscribe (copy plus keep a master reference for future sync) before copying.
attributes: per-plug-in: Yes / No / Copy and Subscribe
workflow: Developer bulk-copies some or all plug-ins from another app, optionally subscribing to keep them updated from the source.
relevance: Same copy/subscribe pattern already logged for every other shared component type; no new information.

name: Creating a REST Source Catalog from OpenAPI
apex: Uploading a single OpenAPI file (or pointing to its URL) auto-generates a full REST Source Catalog, one REST Source template per API operation described, complete with a chosen Default REST Source Type, Default Authentication (with a matching empty credential scaffolded), and an optional Catalog Refresh URL (plus Proxy Server / Web Credential) so the catalog can be re-pulled later to pick up spec changes.
workflow: Developer uploads/points at an OpenAPI spec once, picks sane defaults for type/auth, and gets a whole family of ready-to-use REST Data Source templates instead of defining each endpoint by hand.
relevance: Bulk-generating many data-source templates from one machine-readable spec, with a refreshable link back to the spec, is a good idea if Paddock ever consumes a documented API family (e.g. a motorsport data provider publishing an OpenAPI spec) rather than one-off endpoints.
skip_for_web: None of Paddock's current upstreams (OpenF1, ICS feeds, scrapers) publish OpenAPI specs, so this exact mechanism has no immediate target.

name: Managing Catalog Groups / Exporting and Importing a REST Source Catalog
apex: Catalog Groups are a simple Name+Description folder used purely to organize multiple REST Source Catalogs in the picker; a catalog can be exported to a file and imported into another APEX instance/workspace, then installed either immediately or later from the Export Repository, to move a whole family of REST Data Source templates between environments.
attributes: Install now or later from Export Repository
workflow: Developer groups related catalogs for discoverability and exports a catalog to carry its data-source templates to another environment/workspace.
relevance: A folder-only grouping and a cross-APEX-instance export/import pipeline have no Paddock equivalent (one codebase, one deployment target, no separate 'workspace' concept to move catalogs between).
skip_for_web: Cross-instance catalog portability is APEX-multi-workspace specific.
